name: LOFTY Brickell

why.residential_units: the review's 362 is confirmed by the developer's own general-contractor announcement; the stored 363 came from a two-project round-up
why.contractor: the review's G.T. McDonald Enterprises is confirmed by a dedicated announcement of the appointment. The master permit on this row names GT Construction & Development Inc, but that permit belongs to a DIFFERENT tower — see the note
why.height_ft: 574 ft above ground from the FAA filing, against 579 above sea level
why.name: the parenthetical '(One Brickell Riverfront)' merged two projects into one name

notes: THIS ROW DESCRIBES TWO DIFFERENT TOWERS AND NEEDS SPLITTING — the single biggest open item from this review. Its name, unit count, storey count and height are LOFTY Brickell, a 44-storey tower at 99 SW 7th Street whose $170m construction loan from 3650 REIT closed in July 2022. But its permit anchor, address, floor area, contractor-of-record and lender belong to a later and separate tower: master permit BD22025768001B001 is at 600 SW 1 AV, folio 102051790010, NEW CONSTRUCTION, 853,887 sq ft, $156,263,351, contractor GT Construction & Development Inc, and it was ISSUED ON 18 SEPTEMBER 2025 with work items DOCK, MULTI-FAMILY (CONDO), GENERAL OFFICE, GENERAL RETAIL, CONDO HOTEL and PARKING GARAGE. A permit issued in September 2025 cannot be the tower financed in July 2022. The stored Carlyle Group lender fits the permit rather than the units: it comes from Commercial Observer of 1 Oct 2025 on the Newgard and Two Roads Brickell financing, weeks after that permit issued. Sweeping the feed found NO NEW CONSTRUCTION master permit at 99 SW 7 ST at all, so LOFTY's own permit is either absent from the City's records or filed under a street address not yet identified. WHAT TO DO NEXT: create a row for the 600 SW 1 AV tower (One Brickell Riverfront) carrying the permit, the 853,887 sq ft, GT Construction & Development and Carlyle Group, and leave this row as LOFTY with its 362 units, 44 storeys and 574 ft. That split was not done here because the later tower's own unit count, height and storey count are not in hand and inventing them would be worse than flagging this. The address, floor area, permit number and lender on this row are therefore KNOWINGLY the other tower's and were left untouched rather than deleted. A separate height of 540 ft appears in the December 2023 coverage against the FAA's 574; the FAA figure is explicit about being above ground and is stored, with the 540 recorded here.

name: Okan Tower

why.residential_units: the review's rule is to count every residential unit including condo-hotel units, so the 163 Sky Residences and the 236 condo-hotel residences are both counted; the 316 Hilton keys are not units and stay in the hotel field

notes: UNITS NOW RECORDED as 399, which is the 163 Sky Residences plus the 236 condo-hotel residences. No source prints that total, so it is recorded as a declared sum: both components appear in the one quoted sentence and only the addition is ours. This reverses an earlier deliberate blank, which refused to add the components — the review's rule that condo-hotel units ARE units settles it. The 316-key Hilton hotel stays in the hotel field, because traditional keys are not units. GENERAL CONTRACTOR NOT CHANGED: the review reports Okan Construction, but the City's MASTER building permit BD19018756001B001 — NEW CONSTRUCTION, 914,124 sq ft, $159,980,000, the only master on the folio among 23 building permits — names 1ST UNITED COMPANIES OF SOUTH FLA L.L.C., and the rule is that the contractor comes from the master permit only. The primary record wins, so the stored value stands and the review's figure is recorded here. Worth knowing for context: that master permit is on HOLD and carries no certificate, and the folio's other 22 building permits are shoring, post-tension, curtain wall and phased trade permits whose contractors are subcontractors — Ready Window, Suntech, Power Design, Sprinklermatic.

quotes.residential_units: Once complete, Okan Tower will contain a 316-key Hilton Miami Bayfront Hotel, 236 condo-hotel residences managed by Hilton Hotels & Resorts, 163 Sky Residences, and approximately 64,000 square feet of Class A office space.

name: 1401 Brickell by Santander
notes: FLOOR AREA NOT CHANGED, and this was checked rather than assumed. The review reports Santander's own figure of 1.6 million sq ft against the stored 1,280,763. The stored figure IS the City's master building permit: BD24024742001B001, NEW CONSTRUCTION, TotalSQFT 1,280,763, TotalCost $222,546,101, contractor Coastal Construction, issued and Active with no certificate. The rule is that floor area comes from the master permit, and the primary record wins over a sponsor's press figure, so 1,280,763 stands and Santander's 1.6 million is recorded here. The gap is large enough to be worth one reconciliation — a sponsor's figure often counts the garage and below-grade levels the permit excludes, or counts a gross area the City measures differently. ASSET CLASS CORRECTED to Office in this pass: the master permit's work items are retail, professional office or bank, restaurant and recreation, with no residential token at all, which is also why the unit count is a stated zero rather than a blank.

name: 222 Namdar Towers — Phase II
notes: HEIGHT NOT RECORDED and FLOOR AREA NOT CHANGED. The review reports an FAA approval of 450 ft for this tower. The figure is plausible and may well be right, but the only 450 ft quote in hand belongs to PHASE I — the sentence reads that the FIRST of the 222 Namdar Towers was approved to rise 450 feet — and Phase I is a separate row. Taking Phase I's height for Phase II is exactly the kind of cross-tower borrowing this review is correcting elsewhere, so the field stays empty pending a Phase II-specific FAA case. On floor area: the review reports Florida YIMBY's roughly 395,000 sq ft against the stored 569,969. The stored figure IS the master permit — BD23028187001B001, NEW CONSTRUCTION, 50 NE 3 ST, 569,969 sq ft, $128,663,319, John Moriarty — so the primary record wins. The likely reconciliation is that 395,000 is the residential area and 569,969 the gross including the garage, which the rule says to use. ASSET CLASS CORRECTED to Multifamily Rental in this pass.

name: Midtown 7
notes: STATUS CONFIRMED UNDER CONSTRUCTION, which answers the review's doubt in the opposite direction from what it expected. An issued main building permit is the review's own test for Under Construction, and the absence of any certificate rules out Complete. ASSET CLASS CORRECTED to Multifamily Rental in this pass.

name: JEM Miami Worldcenter
notes: UNITS NOT CHANGED and FLOOR AREA NOT CHANGED, both for want of a quotable source rather than for disagreement. The review reports 789 units as 259 condominiums plus 530 rentals, against the stored 273, and about 1.29 million sq ft against the stored 741,252. The unit figure is very likely right and the stored 273 looks like one component of a two-tower programme — but no source sentence naming both 259 and 530 was retrieved before the research budget for this pass ran out, and this project's units are now recorded as a declared sum only when each component appears in the quote. On floor area the stored 741,252 IS the master permit BD23029000001B001's TotalSQFT, so the primary record stands; if the project is genuinely two towers with two master permits then the row needs splitting and the second permit's area belongs to the second row, which is the same pattern found on the LOFTY row. ASSET CLASS: Mixed-Use is correct and unchanged — a project with both condominiums and rentals is the review's own test for a real second programme. NEXT STEP: one fetch of the JEM programme announcement to quote 259 and 530 in a single sentence, then store 789 as a declared sum.

name: The Residences at Mandarin Oriental, Miami — South Tower
notes: HEIGHT LEFT AT 856 FT AND THE CONFLICT RECORDED. The review reports 826 ft from the permit against the stored 856 ft. The stored figure comes from FAA determination 2026-ASO-7021-OE, whose prose reads that the proposed building project consists of four points at height of 852 and 856 feet AGL, 861 and 865 feet AMSL — an explicit above-ground statement in a primary record. That determination was issued 29 September 2026, which is LATER than this tower's master permit of 16 July 2026, and the rule is that the latest primary document wins. So 856 stands. The review's 826 is recorded here because a 30 ft gap between a permit document and an FAA filing is worth one reconciliation: the likeliest explanation is that the permit states height to a roof or parapet while the FAA states top of structure. NEIGHBOURHOOD SET to Brickell Key in this pass, matching the North Tower on the same island.
